clue.text: Dreadful crank with nothing but funny dance music

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a bad way, so the letters are knocked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O
droll means amusing in a dry way

explanation.surface: A grumble about some awful eccentric who only plays silly dance tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: The O for nothing joins the crank before the shuffle; DROLL is added unchanged afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock and roll is a 1950s genre of popular music made for energetic dancing.

clue.text: Twin asteroids named after city's founders

blocks.note: first meaning: the paired moonlets of the asteroid Sylvia carry these names
second meaning: the legendary twins who founded Rome

explanation.surface: An astronomy note: two paired space rocks were christened after the legendary founders of a city.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is essentially true: the two small moons of asteroid 87 Sylvia were named after Rome's mythical twin founders, so both halves describe the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend the twins raised by a she-wolf founded Rome, and astronomers borrowed their names for a pair of small bodies.

clue.text: Hold tight to club and fish

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An angler told to grip a club and a catch firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling is to grasp firmly and not let go, the same idea as holding tight.

clue.text: Method of calculating how gale removed underwear

indicators.note: read as re-moved, the letters are moved about again into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
a bra is an item of women's underwear

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how a strong wind managed to blow someone's underwear off the washing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removed' looks like taking something away, but split as re-moved it asks for the letters of gale to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Algebra is the branch of mathematics that calculates with symbols standing for unknown numbers.

clue.text: Reduce or undo pleats, say

indicators.note: say tells the solver to go by how the phrase is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: to remove pleats would be to de-pleat a garment

explanation.surface: A dressmaker's choice: take a garment in, or unpick its folds.
explanation.walkthrough: The invented verb de-pleat, meaning to take the pleats out, is pronounced just like a real word.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete is to use up or diminish a supply, so it means reduce.

clue.text: In the open, had romantic meetings that were old fashioned

blocks.note: out of doors is in the open
to date someone is to go on romantic meetings

explanation.surface: A couple's open-air courting described as quaint and old-world.
explanation.definitionFit: Something outdated has fallen out of fashion, belonging to an earlier era.

clue.text: Perhaps leave lofty hill with unknown flower

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters could be one arrangement among many possible ones

blocks.note: taken as written
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

explanation.surface: A walker may come down from a high hill bearing a flower nobody can name.
explanation.walkthrough: The Y from unknown joins the three words before all fifteen letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Lily of the valley is a woodland plant with small white bell-shaped scented blooms.

clue.text: Against time, knowing to turn back towards the left

definitions.note: the answer is an adverb or adjective describing such turning

blocks.note: anti means opposed to
a clock tells the time, and to clock is to time something
wise means knowledgeable

explanation.surface: A wily traveller racing the clock and knowing to double back leftwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Anticlockwise is the British form of the American counterclockwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving anticlockwise means rotating opposite to a clock's hands, so the top swings leftward.

clue.text: Bounder to woo in illegal trial

blocks.note: a kangaroo moves by bounding
to court someone is to woo them

explanation.surface: A cad who set out to seduce someone ends up in the dock at an unlawful hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' is old British slang for a cad, which steers away from its literal sense of something that bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A kangaroo court is an unofficial tribunal that ignores proper legal standards.

clue.text: Frozen? Order gin, getting anaesthetised!

definitions.note: loosely matched: the answer is a participle, the definition past

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so these letters are put in a new sequence

blocks.note: frozen fingers have lost all feeling
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cold drinker orders gin to dull the senses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a bar request, but it tells you to rearrange the three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbing means deadening sensation, which is what an anaesthetic does to a patient.

clue.text: Head has two students with a small bone

blocks.note: pate is an old word for the head
L is a learner, so two of them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A head teacher with a pair of pupils, one with a tiny broken bone.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from the L-plates on British learner drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is the kneecap, a small flat bone at the front of the knee joint.

clue.text: The French put out bilge one student at first finds impossible to read

indicators.note: things put out are disturbed and displaced, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: le is French for the
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
L for learner

explanation.surface: A French sailor pumping out bilge-water finds a pupil's scrawl unreadable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' only adds to the surface; all nine letters from the four pieces are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegible handwriting cannot be deciphered, the literal meaning of not being readable.

clue.text: Mango distributed in between

indicators.note: things distributed are spread around, so the letters end up scattered in another order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fruit being shared out among people sitting between each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Among is a preposition meaning surrounded by or in the midst of, much like between.

clue.text: See ship's lack of profit

blocks.note: lo is an old word for look or see
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A shipowner told to look at the vessel's poor accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss is when costs exceed income, the opposite of making a profit.

clue.text: Different aspect tree affords to one making the running

indicators.note: different signals the letters are to be made into something other than they are

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tree seen from a new angle offers something to a runner.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacesetter leads a race and sets its speed; making the running is the idiom for that.

clue.text: Butchering predator, releasing the body's fluid

definitions.note: the answer is a single drop of that fluid

indicators.note: butchering cuts something up, so the letters are chopped and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grisly scene: a hunter's carcass being cut up and bleeding.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests blood; the fluid is actually that of crying.
explanation.definitionFit: A teardrop is a single bead of the salty liquid shed from the eyes.

clue.text: Is it possible for Dickens's little girl to get on with one Italian dish?

blocks.note: can asks whether something is possible
Little Nell is the heroine of The Old Curiosity Shop
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A question whether a small Victorian heroine can have some pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannelloni are large tubes of pasta, stuffed and baked, a classic of Italian cooking.

clue.text: Farmyard sound's existence in the underworld

blocks.note: a low is the moo of cattle
life is existence

explanation.surface: A cow's lowing as the sign of something living down below.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowlife describes criminals collectively, and the underworld is the criminal class.

clue.text: No new tops manufactured continuously

indicators.note: manufactured means made up, so the letters are constructed into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clothing factory's complaint that it has stopped making any fresh garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-stop means without pause or interruption, carrying on all the time.

clue.text: Organised protest where some made more impact than others

indicators.note: some means only part, so the letters lie within a stretch of the clue

blocks.note: the end of made runs into the start of more
surface padding completing the picture

explanation.surface: A rally at which some marchers made more of a mark than others.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo, short for demonstration, is a public march or rally against something.

clue.text: Electrician runs into weir, maybe

indicators.note: maybe hints the letters could just as well be arranged another way

blocks.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tradesman sprints into a river dam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like it puts one piece inside another, but simply putting R inside weir gives nonsense; the five letters must be rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A wirer is one who installs electrical wiring, which is the job of an electrician.

clue.text: Sadly wino began in a camper

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters fall into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunkard's sorry new life starting off living in a camper.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnebago is an American brand of motorhome, so the name is used for a camper van generally.

clue.text: Go in with some who have driven terribly badly

indicators.note: some means a portion only, so the letters are part of a longer stretch

blocks.note: the end of driven runs into the start of terribly

explanation.surface: An invitation to come aboard with motorists who have just driven atrociously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' looks like an anagram signal but it only supplies letters; 'badly' just pads the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter is to come or go into a place.

clue.text: Mother's return to old town with a single old soldier

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: ma is mother, plus the possessive s
Ur was an ancient Mesopotamian city
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A mother goes back to an old town with a lone veteran.
explanation.definitionFit: A samurai was a member of Japan's feudal warrior class, a soldier of former times.

clue.text: Bird under low angled radar initially named

indicators.note: initially points to the beginnings of the words it follows

blocks.note: the tit is a small songbird
the opening letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: A small bird flying beneath an awkwardly tilted radar beam.
explanation.definitionFit: A titular post exists in name only, carrying a title without real power.

clue.text: Will meal do for a social occasion?

blocks.note: supper is an evening meal
a do is informal British for a party

explanation.surface: A host wondering whether simply feeding guests counts as entertaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will meal do' reads as asking if a meal is enough; 'do' is actually the noun for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A supper party is an evening gathering of guests over a meal, a kind of social event.
